chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Ishaq, from Al-Hasan ibn Abi Al-Hasan Al-Farsi, from Abdullah ibn Al-Hasan ibn Zayd ibn Ali ibn Al-Husayn, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'In the case of a man who bought a slave with a condition of three days, and the slave died during the condition period, it is said: He is sworn by Allah that he was pleased (with the slave), and then he is free from liability (guarantee).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a slave dies during the trial period of a sale?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq clarifies the ruling of *khiyar al-shart* (option of trial) in slave sales, emphasizing that the buyer's liability is contingent upon the absence of hidden defects. The requirement of an oath (*yamin*) serves as a legal presumption of good faith, protecting the buyer from financial loss (*daman*) if the slave dies naturally during the agreed-upon three-day inspection period. This reflects the Shia juristic principle that risk transfers only after the buyer's satisfaction is verified through such oaths or explicit acceptance.
